item.title: Palo Alto leaders condemn ICE violence, consider local protections
item.description: In response to the latest fatal shooting, Palo Alto leaders are strategizing in case the city were ever to find itself in the same situation as Minneapolis. The post Palo Alto leaders condemn ICE violence, consider local protections appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: Attorneys deliver closing statements in Stanford vandalism trial
item.description: Attorneys concluded on Friday their closing statements in the felony trial against five Stanford University students. The post Attorneys deliver closing statements in Stanford vandalism trial appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.description: Read about the reopening of Hoover Elementary School after a major renovation and the school district’s plans for allowing students to skip a math class. The post Around Town: Hoover Elementary reopens, skipping math appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: Santa Clara County may ditch camera vendor amid privacy issues
item.description: Cities across Silicon Valley may be on the cusp of cutting ties with a surveillance company linked to local police departments’ cooperation with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. The post Santa Clara County may ditch camera vendor amid privacy issues appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: February tips for your Peninsula garden: Grafting basics, planting summer seeds, managing weeds
item.description: Did you know that most fruit trees are grafted? Grafting is a technique where tissues from two compatible plants are joined so that they can grow together. Find out how to graft your own trees. The post February tips for your Peninsula garden: Grafting basics, planting summer seeds, managing weeds appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: Police: Jogger killed after Friday car collision

item.title: City Council praises Town & Country’s growing housing proposal
item.description: The developers behind a proposal for two seven-story apartment buildings on the northernmost surface parking lot at Town & Country Village received positive initial feedback from the Palo Alto City Council on Monday night, even after announcing that the 158-unit project could expand to 200 or more. The post City Council praises Town & Country’s growing housing proposal appeared first on Palo Alto Online.
